hook: Forgotten voices from Frank Lloyd Wright's inner circle were finally unlocked in 2026.

sections.voiceover: Forgotten voices from Frank Lloyd Wright's inner circle were finally unlocked in 2026.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of a 2026 date stamp on a digital archive interface.

sections.voiceover: But how did these fragile recordings survive decades of storage in the University at Buffalo archives?
sections.visual_cue: Archive storage shelves at the University at Buffalo showing manuscript MS 22.93.

sections.voiceover: The collection includes firsthand accounts from Darwin R. Martin, the son of Wright's famous client. These interviews feature family members sharing rare insights into the architect's residential design process.
sections.visual_cue: Archival photograph of Darwin R. Martin, born in 1900.

sections.voiceover: The University at Buffalo preserves these interviews under manuscript number MS 22.93 for public access.
sections.visual_cue: Historical image of the William R. Heath House in Buffalo.

sections.voiceover: This collection remains a vital link to Wright's work recorded between 1971 and 1980.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of a vintage reel-to-reel tape machine spinning.
